flags.title: Valuation blind-spot
flags.note: Rich valuation — P/E 15, P/B 2.8, DCF overvalued 37%. A market-beating chart doesn't make a rich entry safe; the price already discounts a lot of the good news.
flags.lesson: KPIT: strong EV/software story, valuation ignored → about −30%.

flags.title: Chasing strength
flags.note: Extended — 90% up its 52-week range, RS 100, -4% from the high. Momentum isn't an edge by itself — define risk/stop before chasing.
flags.lesson: The market prices expectations; a late entry carries the drawdown, not the edge.

flags.title: Sector tailwind
flags.note: Chemicals is in a TAILWIND (tailwind score +0.76) — the macro backdrop supports the setup.
flags.lesson: Focus on cycles and change, not insider chatter (the author's actual edge).

flags.title: Size it — don't fall in love
flags.note: Even a clean BUY deserves a position cap and an exit plan. Concentrated conviction (loyalty to one name) is how good theses become big drawdowns.
flags.lesson: Amazon: a great company held with no diversification became the biggest single loss.

threats.point: The domestic ABS business is exposed to foreign exchange risks as key raw materials like Styrene and Acrylonitrile are entirely imported.
threats.evidence: Risk disclosed in the filings: "The ABS business in India is exposed to the risk of foreign exchange fluctuations, as the key raw materials viz. ‘Styrene’ and ‘Acrylonitrile’ are import dependent, as there is no indigenous producer for these monomers." (annual report - 2026-03-31)
